title: Build a local image
summary: docker build reads a Dockerfile and its build context. -t gives the resulting image a tag.
introduction: docker build reads a Dockerfile and its build context. -t gives the resulting image a tag. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: docker build reads a Dockerfile and its build context. -t gives the resulting image a tag.
The dot means the current directory is the build context. Build this only inside the intended practice folder.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Identify where the Dockerfile and index.html must be.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A large or secret-filled build context can include files you did not intend to send to the builder.
For more detail later, use this [Docker further reading](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/).

seo.title: Docker: Build a local image
seo.description: Learn about build a local image in Docker. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
